title: In West Bank, date farmers weigh impact of UK sanctions on Israeli settlers
summary:
Juicy brown and ripening yellow dates dangle down from the branches of each palm tree at Israeli settler farms in the Jordan Valley, in the occupied West Bank.
This year, as Israeli growers get ready for a good harvest, they are also preparing for the impact of new Western sanctions against settlements, which are illegal under international law.
Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden have also confirmed their intention to introduce national restrictions, or support European restrictions, on trade in goods with settlements.
Israeli date farmer Avigdor Arbel, from the settlement of Mesua, calls such boycotts "really disgusting".
However, he says the sector is ready for any new UK ban on settler goods.

title: Russia markets drone-like missiles in Egypt during Su-57 jet's Africa air show debut
summary:
EL ALAMEIN, Egypt, Sept 9 (Reuters) - Russian state-owned arms exporter Rosoboronexport showed off drone-like missiles for its Sukhoi Su-57 fifth-generation stealth ‌jet fighter in Egypt on Wednesday as the warplane made its ‌African air show debut.
The jet roared over the arid landscape outside the El Alamein International ​Airport near the Mediterranean coast during the second installment of an exhibition meant to position Egypt as a gateway to African and Middle Eastern markets.
On display in Russia's section of the airfield were S-71M and S-71K missiles, which combine ‌features of cruise missiles and ⁠low-cost attack drones, according to defence industry outlets.
Ukraine said it hit an Su-57 at an air base inside Russia in 2024.
Mohammed Al-Sayed, a consultant at the Egyptian private defence company Amstone International Group, ​said turnout reflected interest ‌in Egypt as a gateway to African and Arab defence ​markets.

title: Houthi attacks disrupt Saudi energy facilities, wound 73, authorities say
summary:
Sept 8 (Reuters) - Operations at some energy facilities in Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, were halted on Tuesday following attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis that wounded 73 people, in what ‌Saudi authorities described as a dangerous escalation.
Fires erupted at the sites and several people were injured as ‌firefighting and other emergency teams rushed to contain the blazes and assess the damage, the Saudi energy ministry said.
Brent crude futures rose $1 ⁠to $98 a barrel after the Saudi energy ministry statement, while U.S. crude futures rose over $2 to $93.65 a barrel.
On Monday, the Financial Times newspaper said Aramco's Jazan ​oil ​facilities were hit in new strikes, and the damage was ​being assessed.
The Saudi energy ministry said concerned authorities were dealing with the repercussions of the attacks.

title: Russia and North Korea open the first road across their shared border
summary:
Russia and North Korea open the first road across their shared bordertoggle caption Dmitry Ignatenko/Government of Primorsky Krai Reg/via APRussia and North Korea opened the first road bridge across their shared border Monday, a development that both countries hailed as boosting their deepening ties.
The bridge links North Korea's Rason and Russia's Khasan, border cities of the two countries.
Relations and exchange programs between Russia and North Korea have been flourishing, with North Korea supplying ammunition and troops to support Russia's war against Ukraine in return for economic and military assistance.
North Korea has been receiving Russian tourists since February 2024 amid slowly easing pandemic curbs.
North Korea and Russia, which are already served by a railway bridge and air service, agreed in 2024 to construct a bridge for automobiles over the Tumen River, which runs along North Korea's borders with Russia and China.

title: UK government expected to announce restrictions on trade with West Bank settlements
summary:
The UK government is to set out new restrictions on buying goods made in Jewish settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, the BBC understands.
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is expected to outline the measures in the Commons on Tuesday, which could include restrictions on trade in agricultural products from settlements.
Settlements are illegal under international law, and recent months have seen a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the West Bank by settlers.
One minister told the BBC: "The statement will be a complete reset of the nature of our Israel-Palestine relationship.
But Labour MPs who have been briefed on the plans believe the sanctions will target trade with illegal settlements.

title: Iceland summons US ambassador over Trump's stars and stripes map
summary:
Iceland has summoned the US ambassador after President Donald Trump posted a map on social media that appeared to show Iceland and several other countries covered by the American flag.
Trump posted the image on Truth Social on Monday, showing the US, Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean covered in stars and stripes.
Iceland's foreign minister said the post was "completely inappropriate".
Responding to Trump's post, Iceland's Foreign Minister Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir called in US ambassador to Iceland Billy Long, who formally took up the post last month, local media reported.
"Proudly we are a free, independent, and sovereign nation," she wrote on social media.

summary:

title: Hungary expels 10 Russian diplomats as relations with Kremlin worsen
summary:
Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orbán says 10 Russian diplomats have been ordered to leave Budapest for taking part in "unacceptable" activities.
The Hungarian foreign minister said the decision to expel the diplomats "does not imply breaking off diplomatic relations with Russia", but the foreign ministry spokeswoman in Moscow said "the response to the Russophobic lobby will be harsh and painful".
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar promised "pragmatic" relations with Moscow from the moment his Tisza party was elected in April.
He and the foreign minister have both called on Russia to bring an end to the war in Ukraine.
In May Anita Orbán summoned the Russian ambassador to protest against a big drone attack on the Transcarpathia region of Ukraine that is home to a large Hungarian minority.

summary:

title: Nuclear watchdog refers Iran to UN Security Council over 'non-compliance'
summary:
The UN nuclear watchdog has referred Iran to the Security Council for "non-compliance" with its obligations under the non-proliferation treaty - the first such move in 20 years.
It cites a lack of information on Iran's nuclear material such as its stockpile of highly enriched uranium, and the lack of access to nuclear facilities for IAEA inspectors.
Tehran condemned the IAEA decision, blaming US and Israeli strikes on its nuclear facilities for disrupting inspections.
The IAEA resolution - tabled by the UK, France, Germany and the US - was backed by 23 countries, with eight abstentions.
At the start of the latest US-Israel war against Iran, Tehran had roughly 440kg (970lb) of 60% enriched uranium, according to senior US officials.

summary:

title: War of words between China and Philippines over South China Sea claims
summary:
BANGKOK (AP) — China on Wednesday accused the Philippines of "stirring up trouble" after harsh words from Philippines Defense Minister Gilberto Teodoro Jr. over Beijing's increasingly aggressive pursuit of maritime claims in the South China Sea.
"We urge the relevant people in the Philippines to stop seeking attention and stirring up trouble and to cease undermining China-Philippines relations and stability in the South China Sea," Mao told reporters in Beijing after recapitulating the official position.
A tribunal established in The Hague under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea ruled in 2016 that China's claims in the South China Sea are illegal.
In July, the U.S., Britain, and a dozen other Western and Asian countries issued a joint statement reasserting that China's claims in the South China Sea were illegal based upon the ruling issued a decade earlier.

title: Putin assures Trump that Moscow doesn’t have aggressive plans toward Europe, Kremlin says
summary:
KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Russian President Vladimir Putin assured U.S. President Donald Trump in a phone call Tuesday that Moscow doesn't harbor aggressive intentions toward Europe, a senior Kremlin official said, after European officials blamed Moscow for sabotage campaigns on their soil.
U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff visited Moscow and Kyiv for separate talks with Putin and Zelenskyy over the weekend.
The Kremlin says call between Putin and Trump was 'constructive'Yuri Ushakov, Putin's foreign affairs adviser, said the hourlong conversation between Putin and Trump was "constructive and quite frank."
The proposals will remain under wraps for now, he said, but he expressed hope that talks involving delegations from Ukraine, Russia and the U.S. can take place in the fall.
